name: FreeImage
listed_description: An open source library that supports popular graphics image formats and others as needed by today's multimedia applications.
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline found. SourceForge project page (https://sourceforge.net/projects/freeimage/) makes no speed claims; searches for FreeImage load or resize benchmarks against libjpeg-turbo, libpng, stb_image, DevIL, ImageMagick, OpenCV returned nothing that includes FreeImage. freeimage.sourceforge.net redirects to freeimage.sourceforge.io which is unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). It wraps libjpeg, libpng and libtiff rather than competing with them.

name: FreeType
listed_description: FreeType is a freely available software library to render fonts.
reason: No numeric comparison against an external baseline. README says only 'small, efficient, highly customizable'. docs/CHANGES (read in full by grep) has speedups only against earlier FreeType versions (e.g. TrueType interpreter 15% faster, BDF loader 75% faster, GPOS kerning 3.5x faster). Third-party numbers found (ttf-parser outlining benchmark via search snippet: FreeType 1.26 ms vs stb_truetype 0.7 ms on glyf, 4-6 ms vs 2.9 ms on CFF) show FreeType slower, and the fontdue README charts are images with no numbers. freetype.org is unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND www.freetype.org) and freetype-demos on GitHub returned 404.

name: GDCM
reason: No benchmark in the repo, README or SourceForge tree (README covers build and nightly testing only; gdcm.sourceforge.net wiki main page returned 404). Only quantitative hit is a 2010 ITK mailing-list thread seen via search snippet (ITK 3.18 + GDCM 2.0 faster than ITK 3.18's own reader on little-endian DICOM but slower on JPEG files, Windows XP); the thread host itk.org is unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) so it could not be opened or quoted, and no table numbers were obtained.

name: GLFW
listed_description: A simple, cross-platform OpenGL wrangling library
reason: No numeric comparison. README and repo page describe a window, context and input library with no benchmarks or speed claims against SDL or any other library.

name: GLFWPP
listed_description: A thin modern C++17 header-only wrapper for GLFW
reason: No numbers. README says only that overhead 'should be low' because the wrapper is thin, with no measurement; it notes glfw::Event uses std::function, which it calls slow, and that exceptions cost only on the error path. Directional claim without numbers.

name: graphene
listed_description: Thin layer of graphical data types
reason: No numeric comparison. README describes SSE2, SSE 4.1, ARM NEON and GCC vector-extension fast paths against a scalar fallback but gives no timings, and compares against no other maths library (GLM, DirectXMath, etc.). The README mentions a benchmark suite and -Dbenchmarks=false, but the current meson_options.txt has no benchmarks option and no benchmark files appear in tests/ or src/ listings. A web search for published SIMD-versus-scalar numbers found none.
